what_i_see: A bright, smooth, red elliptical galaxy with an extended halo fills the field. About 2.4 arcsec south-west of its core is a faint, thin streak, roughly 1.5 arcsec long. It shows up mainly in VIS, looks slightly bluish in the colour tile, and lies roughly tangential to the galaxy. No counter-image is obvious. The surrounding field contains ordinary small galaxies.
most_likely: A faint edge-on or elongated background galaxy seen through the elliptical's halo by chance. A weakly lensed or strongly lensed arc from a luminous early-type at photo-z about 0.28 is the alternative.
against_it: The streak is thin, bluish and roughly tangential at a radius that suits a massive elliptical's Einstein radius, which a lens would produce. But it is a single feature with no counter-image and needs sigma near 340 km/s.
decisive_test: Subtract a smooth model of the elliptical in VIS to look for a counter-image or curvature. Or take a spectrum of the streak to see whether its redshift is well above 0.28.
catalogue_notes: Host galaxy WISEA J041300.68-525302.4 (Gaia DR3 4780238406483345664, G=21.1, no parallax) is 2.4 arcsec NE. LS DR10 lists it as SER, r=18.0, z_phot=0.28. Nothing in SIMBAD within 60 arcsec, no DES/DECaLS lens catalogue hits within 30-60 arcsec, and no Abell or redMaPPer cluster within 5 arcmin.
